title: Metaprobe Orchestrator and Adaptive Resampling Manifest
author: Chen Li
body:
Summary:

This page describes the Metaprobe Orchestrator: an evaluation mediation layer that dynamically selects, resamples, and routes probes across the eval fleet to optimize coverage, cost, and signal freshness for model onboarding, quantization profiling, and regression triage. The document covers architecture, scheduling policies, scoring heuristics, telemetry signals, an operational runbook for probe-driven regressions, and an onboarding checklist for teams integrating with the orchestrator.

Motivation:

- Eval teams must balance probe coverage (breadth/depth) with constrained compute budget and sensitivity to recent traffic patterns.
- Existing static probe rotations create stale signals and duplicated work across onboarding, quantization, and shadow validation.
- The Metaprobe Orchestrator (MPO) unifies probe selection and sampling so a single source of truth can: reduce noise, prioritize high-value probes, and speed up regression detection.

Scope and non-goals:

- In-scope: interactive evals, batch probes, shadow traffic mirroring, probe resampling for quant/kv-cache sensitivity, prioritization for rare-slice detection.
- Out of scope: annotator UI, human label workflows (these remain in Annotator Service), direct model training pipelines.

Key definitions:

- Probe family: a templated set of inputs targeting a semantic slice (e.g., payment-instruments, long-context-coherence).
- Metaprobe manifest: a declarative YAML that describes families, weight policy, freshness window, and acceptance criteria.
- Resampling: changing the selection of concrete probes from a family in response to telemetry (errors, drift, token-costs).

Architecture overview (textual diagram):

MPO Controller -> Scheduler -> Scoring Engine -> Eval Mesh (worker pool) -> Results Stores + Telemetry PubSub

- Controller: accepts manifests and exposes APIs for onboarding and weight adjustments.
- Scheduler: maps families to compute slots respecting tenant and budget constraints.
- Scoring Engine: computes a per-probe utility score using telemetry and meta-features.
- Eval Mesh: fleet of evaluators (interactive, batch, shadow) executing probes.

Probe manifest: authoritative example (YAML-like):

- name: long_context_anchor
  families: [long-context, prefix-priming]
  target_rps: 2
  freshness_window_minutes: 60
  max_daily_tokens: 100000
  priority_tiers: [critical, standard]
  detection_contracts: [coherence-drop>=0.2, latency_tail>=250ms]

Prioritization and scoring heuristic:

Score(p) = w1 * recent_delta + w2 * severity + w3 * entropy_gain - w4 * cost_penalty

Where:
- recent_delta: normalized change in probe metric vs baseline (0..1).
- severity: categorical mapping (critical=1, high=0.75, standard=0.4).
- entropy_gain: anticipated information gain from running the probe (higher for rare slices).
- cost_penalty: per-token and runtime cost estimated by the runtime estimator.

Default weight recommendations (tunable per team):

- w1: 0.45, w2: 0.25, w3: 0.2, w4: 0.1

Scheduling policy (multi-tenant constrained):

1. Reserve 30% of budget for critical-tier probes and regressions.
2. Use priority queue by Score(p) across families; break ties by multicast diversity (spread probes across tenants).
3. Enforce per-team daily token cap and soft throttles at 90% consumption.

Telemetry signals used for scoring and resampling:

- Response quality deltas (coherence, factuality, rerank precision).
- Latency SLO violations (p95 >= configured threshold).
- Token consumption trending (7d moving average).
- Shadow mismatch frequency (shadow vs prod).
- KV-cache hit rate sensitivity (for long-context families).

Integration points (APIs & contracts):

- /manifests (POST/GET/PUT): register or update metaprobe manifests.
- /score-feedback (POST): ingest probe results and derived metrics to update the scoring model.
- /schedule-status (GET): returns scheduled probe batches and backlog.

Example CLI onboarding flow:

1) Team prepares manifest file: myfamily.manifest.yaml
2) Register: redwood-mpo register --manifest myfamily.manifest.yaml --owner team-x
3) Warmup run: redwood-mpo run --manifest myfamily --mode shadow --samples 50
4) Promote to continuous scheduling after 48h of stable fidelity metrics.

Onboarding checklist (condensed):

- Define families and detection contracts.
- Set target_rps and max_daily_tokens.
- Provide baseline metrics and golden traces.
- Assign oncall owner and escalation path.
- Run 48-hour warmup with shadow mode and sanity checks.

Operational runbook: regression triggered by probe signal

1. Alert: SQC (service quality contract) alert fires when Score(p) > 0.8 and severity >= high.
2. Initial Triage (15m): owner reviews failing probes, compares to baseline, and identifies affected slices.
3. Isolation (30m): schedule focused replay on dev mesh with deterministic seeds and increased sampling for the failing family.
4. Blame surface (1–4h): run causal bisect using: 1) model version, 2) quant profile, 3) runtime kernel selection, 4) prompt template changes.
4a. If quant profile implicated, trigger quant-safety rollback (see quant rollback contract).
4b. If prompt or template changes implicated, open a prompt-fix PR and block rollout.
5. Mitigation & Rollback (24h): apply mitigations — fallback to verified variant, pin model, or degrade QoS with communication.
6. Postmortem: owner writes a short incident summary and attaches the manifest, logs, and sample artifacts to the incident.

Runbook thresholds and SLOs (suggested):

- Probe freshness: 60m (run frequency for critical probes).
- Regression detection latency: detect within 30m for critical slices.
- False positive rate target: <= 5% (via ensemble checks).
- Budget adherence: soft throttle at 90% daily cap, hard throttle at 100%.

Quantization and KV-cache interplay:

- MPO must annotate probes with quant-sensitivity flags. If a probe signals coherence regression only under quantized variant, the scoring engine escalates to the Quant Audit Queue and triggers prioritized shadow replays with mixed-precision settings.
- KV-cache-sensitive probes are marked with a context_seed and increase sampling of long prefixes; scheduler enforces prefix-priming runs to reproduce cache behavior.

Data artifacts and storage:

- Results store schema (columns): probe_id | family | model_version | quant_profile | timestamp | metrics_json | raw_response_ref
- Retention policy: probe meta and scores retained 180 days; raw annotated responses retained 30 days by default.

Safety and noise-reduction practices:

- Ensemble validation: run 3 independent probe seeds and require consensus for high-severity alerts.
- Anchor-based baselining: compute baseline using 7-day rolling anchor set and require delta > threshold on two consecutive windows before firing critical alerts.
- Cost gating: probes with projected per-sample cost > X tokens or runtime > Y ms require explicit owner approval.

Example score-feedback payload (pseudo-YAML for /score-feedback):

probe_id: lp-2026-02-18-001
family: long_context_anchor
metrics:
  coherence_delta: 0.25
  p95_latency_ms: 320
  token_cost: 112
model_version: v3.4-rc2

Operational metrics dashboard (suggested widgets):

- Probe throughput by family (timeseries)
- Regression heatmap: family x model_version (cells show detection rate)
- Token spend per-team (rolling 24h)
- Shadow mismatch frequency by region

Migration & backward compatibility:

- MPO supports an import compatibility shim: legacy probe manifests (v1) are converted to v2 with a default scoring mapping.
- Policy: new scoring models roll out under a canary flag for 7 days and must show stable false positive rates before global enablement.

Roles and ownership:

- MPO Core (team): Applied ML infrastructure — primary owner for controller, scoring engine, and scheduler.
- Onboarding team (requester): owns manifest correctness, golden baseline, and annotation contracts.
- Observability (team): owns dashboards, alerting rules, and retention policy.

Open design questions (to resolve before GA):

- Optimal information-gain estimator for rare slices (ML research action).
- Dynamic weight tuning: whether to learn weights w1..w4 from labeled regression outcomes.
- Cross-tenant fairness: policy for how to interleave probes when multiple tenants compete for rare-slice coverage.

Appendix: example manifest tuning recommendations:

| field | recommendation | rationale |
|---|---|---|
| freshness_window_minutes | 60 for critical, 180 for standard | faster detection for critical slices |
| max_daily_tokens | 100k default, set per-team | keep predictable budget |
| priority_tiers | critical/standard/low | helps scheduler reserve budget |

References and related pages:

- See eval-harness probe scheduling standards for low-latency shadowing.
- Quantization profiles: refer to per-workload quant tuner guide for sensitivity thresholds.

Contact & escalation:

- MPO Core oncall: @applied-ml-infra-oncall
- For urgent regressions: ping the Observability SRE rotation and create a P1 in the incident tracker.
